newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE to settle back to near 4,325-4,330.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE to settle back to near 4,325-4,330.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index may settle back to around 4,325-4,330 and then flatten out on Wednesday, technical analysts said.
Its roaring finish on Tuesday in pursuit of new record highs will be met by a less confident tone in the market today, they added.

Obliged to step back a pace after the uncomfortable retreat on Wall street last night, the FTSE will reject any chance to spurt forward today as technically the breadth and pace from Tuesday cannot be sustained for a second day.
By 0814 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 9.9 at 4,347.8.
Market breadth for the FTSE as measured by the advance/decline ratio for stocks within it was a healthy five-to-one on Tuesday in favour of advancing stocks as the index hurtled up some 50 points.
Such one day swings are largely uncontrollable -- at least without the support from Wall Street -- so that at best the FTSE may mark time at around 4,330, analysts said.

And as the market cools down from Tuesday's excesses this should allow investors time to readjust their portfolios which will introduce more stock rotation and will put on hold any ambitions the market may have for setting new highs.

Analysts noted that in the broader market, shares in the healthcare and pharmaceuticals sectors, which had been strong a few weeks ago, have given up some of the running to the oil explorers and building materials groups.
Retail stocks have not kept pace with the market recently and these look vulnerable, they added.
